title: A posture, a pause
alt: A woman in a dark jacket and ivory trousers sits to the left of a sunlit wall; the empty wall occupies almost half the composition.
note: The empty wall is active space. Keeping the chair and the cast light in the frame makes the posture feel situated, rather than isolated.

crops.title: Bring the posture forward
crops.alt: Square crop of the seated woman, bringing her face, hands and folded trousers closer while removing much of the wall.
crops.note: A square edit brings the face, hands and folded trousers into one compact reading. It gains intimacy and gives up the breathing room of the original.

crops.title: Let absence take the lead
crops.alt: Crop of the empty chair edge, a sliver of dark clothing and a large sunlit wall.
crops.note: Moving attention toward the wall makes the figure partial. The chair edge becomes a trace of presence; use this as a pause after the full scene, not as a replacement portrait.

title: The weight of a fold
alt: A woman turns her head while lifting ivory fabric at both shoulders; soft folds cross her torso against a warm grey wall.
note: The full portrait holds the relationship between the turned head, raised hands and falling cloth. Its vertical format lets the fabric carry the movement.

crops.title: Follow the turn
crops.alt: Close crop around the turned head, shoulders and raised hand holding pale fabric.
crops.note: Removing the lower fabric directs attention to the turn of the head and the hand at the shoulder. The composition becomes a gesture of attention rather than a study of the garment.

crops.title: Read the material
crops.alt: Close crop of overlapping ivory folds across a torso, with the face outside the frame.
crops.note: Taking the face out of the frame changes the subject to light and material. The diagonal fold carries the eye across the edit; this detail belongs beside its parent image.

title: A stem holds the room
alt: A burgundy anthurium leans above a clear glass of water on a pale stone block, with rumpled linen to the left and a small stone to the right.
note: A narrow stem connects two different visual weights: the dark flower above and the glass below. The linen and stone keep the arrangement from becoming perfectly symmetrical.

crops.title: Keep the vertical conversation
crops.alt: A closer vertical crop showing the burgundy flower, its thin stem and the top of the clear water glass.
crops.note: This tighter vertical edit keeps the flower and water connected while removing the pedestal. It makes the fragile stem more prominent and the setting less important.

crops.title: Give weight to the base
crops.alt: Horizontal crop of the water glass, rumpled linen, small stone and rough edge of the pale block; the flower is outside the frame.
crops.note: The base edit exchanges the flower for three surfaces: glass, linen and stone. Their different edges and textures become the subject. The absent flower is understood through the original.

title: Objects in conversation
alt: A pale sculptural vase, leafy branch, cut pomegranates and a stemmed glass sit on a cloth-covered table in diagonal sunlight.
note: The vase anchors the left side while the branch reaches right. The glass and fruit bridge their different scales. A diagonal band of light ties the objects together.

crops.title: Collect the visual weight
crops.alt: Close crop of the vase base, open pomegranate and glass on the linen-covered table.
crops.note: The lower, wider edit gathers the vase, glass and fruit into a dense cluster. It strengthens material relationships while reducing the original's airy branch and wall.

crops.title: Let light organize the image
crops.alt: Vertical crop of the glass and hanging branch beneath a diagonal band of sunlight, with the large vase outside the frame.
crops.note: Removing the heavy vase leaves the branch and glass suspended across the light. The diagonal now organizes the image. Compare the quieter balance with the clustered object edit.

title: A room held by light
alt: An empty wooden chair stands beside a tall opening in a warm stone room; a sharp triangle of sunlight crosses the wall and floor.
note: The opening, chair and triangle of light establish three different geometries. Keeping them together makes the empty space feel inhabited without adding a figure.

crops.title: Make a threshold
crops.alt: Tall narrow crop of the room's open doorway, outside tree and light falling onto the stone floor; the chair is excluded.
crops.note: This tall edit removes the chair and lets the opening become a threshold. The vertical edge frames a small glimpse outside, while the floor light keeps the space connected.

crops.title: Give absence a scale
crops.alt: Vertical crop around the empty wooden chair and triangular wall light, without the doorway.
crops.note: The chair gives the room a human scale even when no person is present. Removing the opening concentrates the relationship between its rigid edges and the sloping light.

crops.title: Follow the light across
crops.alt: Wide crop showing the chair, doorway edge and bands of light and shadow crossing the floor.
crops.note: The wider floor edit connects opening and chair through shadow. It changes a vertical room into a horizontal sequence, useful as a closing image after the more enclosed crops.
